recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV elevated (+11.7% vs baseline) but sleep severely deficient (4.1h avg, 13/14 nights <7h), resting HR down (-2.3 bpm) — likely fatigue masking as 'recovery' due to autonomic dysregulation

readiness.guidance: Prioritise sleep consolidation and nervous system restoration over volume or intensity; avoid any Z4+ efforts until sleep stabilises ≥6.5h/night and HRV remains stable for 5+ days.

monthly_review.summary: July shows a clear volume rebound (+9.6 km) and pace acceleration (+18 sec/km faster than June), but at the cost of increased aerobic strain (aerobic TE up from 2.7 to 3.1) and higher Z3–Z4 distribution — a shift toward threshold work without commensurate recovery support.
monthly_review.highlight: The 18-sec/km pace improvement from June to July is real and reinforced by multi-month trend: pace has accelerated every month since March (551 → 532 → 534 → 539 → 521), yet this acceleration coincides with rising aerobic TE and falling cadence — indicating growing effort cost per unit speed.

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s distance (70.6 vs 61.0 km) and need no additional running in the final 4 days — especially given compromised readiness. Chasing more volume would risk undermining the aerobic gains you’ve built.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt correlates with reduced running economy stability
insights.body: Despite stable median running economy (257.0 ml/kg/km), recent values show high volatility (234.6 → 262.2 → 257.0) — and 13 of last 14 nights were <7h sleep. Poor sleep impairs neuromuscular coordination, reflected in stride length variability (70.4–89.8 cm across recent runs) and vertical oscillation drift (7.6–8.5 cm).

insights.title: ACWR of 0.8 reflects load reduction — not optimal loading
insights.body: ACWR = 0.8 sits in 'OPTIMAL' band per Garmin, but acute load (192) is 26 points below chronic (218), and last 4 weeks’ TRIMP includes a drastic drop (41) — indicating an abrupt cut, not steady progression. Recovery balance (3.09) is artificially inflated by suppressed load, not robust HRV resilience.

insights.title: Elevated decoupling (7.09%) persists despite VO2max increase
insights.body: VO2max rose +2.8 (36.3 → 39.0), yet latest aerobic decoupling is 7.09% — well above the 5% aerobic-sound threshold — and median recent decoupling is 7.11%. This suggests improved capacity but impaired endurance efficiency, likely tied to sleep debt and inconsistent Z2 base development (Z2 % dropped from 43% in May to 32% in July).

insights.title: Zone 2 efficiency (0.7879 m/beat) lags Zone 1 (0.8319) — base isn’t anchoring
insights.body: The 5.5% drop in efficiency moving from Z1 to Z2 indicates underdeveloped aerobic infrastructure: ideal Z2 should sustain >90% of Z1 efficiency. With Z2 now 32% of July volume (vs 43% in May), this gap implies diminishing returns on moderate-effort work unless Z1 volume rebuilds first.

recommendations.action: Complete two 30-min Zone 1 walks or very easy jogs (HR ≤125 bpm, pace >10:00/km) on July 26 and 28, with strict 7.5+ hours sleep before each.
recommendations.reason: Rebuild autonomic resilience and reinforce Z1 neuromuscular patterning without cardiovascular or metabolic stress — directly addressing low training readiness and high aerobic TE.

recommendations.action: Perform daily 10-min parasympathetic priming: 4-7-8 breathing (4s inhale, 7s hold, 8s exhale) x5 rounds upon waking and 1h before bed.
recommendations.reason: To counteract chronic sleep debt and improve HRV sustainability — recent HRV elevation appears reactive, not restorative; structured vagal tone work supports deeper recovery.

recommendations.action: Skip all structured runs July 27, 29, and 30; replace with mobility drills (calf/hip flexor release + single-leg balance holds) and hydration/nutrition check-in (aim for ≥2.5L water, 30g protein within 30m of waking).
recommendations.reason: Prevent cumulative fatigue from back-to-back sessions while reinforcing recovery behaviours — critical given 13/14 nights <7h sleep and Body Battery deficit.

risk_flags.evidence: HRV up +11.7% but resting HR down -2.3 bpm, sleep <7h on 13/14 nights, training readiness = 30, Body Battery -7.6% — classic signs of sympathetic withdrawal without parasympathetic restoration
risk_flags.action: Pause all HR-based zone training until 5 consecutive nights ≥6.5h sleep AND HRV stays within ±5% of baseline for 3 days

risk_flags.risk: Running economy instability increasing injury susceptibility
risk_flags.evidence: Stride length varies 19.4 cm (70.4–89.8) across last 10 runs; vertical oscillation ranges 7.6–8.5 cm; ground contact time increased to 319 ms on July 12 long run — all reflect neuromuscular inconsistency from sleep debt
risk_flags.action: Replace all non-Z1 running with walking or cycling for 5 days; reintroduce running only after 3 nights ≥7h sleep and stride length CV <5%
